about: The twenty-one ecumenical councils as the Catholic Church counts them, in order. Summaries are written for this site in plain words. 'work' names a reading-room work id; the row shows 'Read on this site' only once that work has a hosted edition in data/library.json. 'links' are outbound links checked when added (see docs/research/councils-sources-2026-11.csv). Rendered by tools/councils_page.py into /councils/ (tools/build_static.py).

councils.name: First Council of Nicaea
councils.summary: Taught, against Arius, that the Son is true God, of one substance with the Father; issued the first form of the Nicene Creed; and set a common way to date Easter.

councils.name: First Council of Constantinople
councils.summary: Confessed the divinity of the Holy Spirit and completed the Creed in the form still prayed at Mass.

councils.name: Council of Ephesus
councils.summary: Rejected the teaching of Nestorius and confessed Mary as Theotokos, Mother of God, because her Son is one divine Person.

councils.name: Council of Chalcedon
councils.summary: Defined that Christ is one Person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion or division, receiving the Tome of Pope Leo the Great.

councils.name: Second Council of Constantinople
councils.summary: Condemned the writings known as the Three Chapters and confirmed the teaching of Chalcedon against a Nestorian reading of it.

councils.name: Third Council of Constantinople
councils.summary: Taught that Christ has two wills, divine and human, the human will always following the divine, against monothelitism.

councils.name: Second Council of Nicaea
councils.summary: Upheld the veneration of holy images, distinguishing the honor shown to them from the worship due to God alone.

councils.name: Fourth Council of Constantinople
councils.summary: Deposed Photius and restored Ignatius as patriarch of Constantinople, and confirmed the veneration of images. It is counted as ecumenical in the West.

councils.name: First Lateran Council
councils.summary: Confirmed the Concordat of Worms, which settled the dispute over lay investiture of bishops, and passed canons of reform.

councils.name: Second Lateran Council
councils.summary: Ended the schism of the antipope Anacletus II and passed canons on the discipline and celibacy of the clergy.

councils.name: Third Lateran Council
councils.summary: Required a two-thirds majority of the cardinals to elect a pope and passed canons against simony and heresy.

councils.name: Fourth Lateran Council
councils.summary: Professed the faith in a creed that uses the word transubstantiation, required yearly confession and Easter Communion, and called a crusade.

councils.name: First Council of Lyon
councils.summary: Declared the Emperor Frederick II deposed and called for help for the Holy Land.

councils.name: Second Council of Lyon
councils.summary: Received a short-lived reunion with the Greek Church, taught that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and set rules for the conclave.

councils.name: Council of Vienne
councils.summary: Suppressed the Knights Templar and taught that the rational soul is of itself the form of the human body.

councils.name: Council of Constance
councils.summary: Ended the Western Schism with the election of Martin V and condemned the teachings of Wycliffe and Hus.

councils.name: Council of Basel, Ferrara, and Florence
councils.summary: Agreed decrees of reunion with the Greeks, Armenians, Copts, and others, and defined the primacy of the Roman Pontiff.

councils.name: Fifth Lateran Council
councils.summary: Taught that each human soul is individual and immortal, and passed reforms on the eve of the Reformation.

councils.name: Council of Trent
councils.summary: Answered the Protestant Reformation on Scripture and Tradition, justification, and the seven sacraments, and began the reform of the clergy and seminaries.

councils.name: First Vatican Council
councils.summary: Taught that God can be known by the light of natural reason, and defined the primacy of the pope and his infallibility when he teaches ex cathedra.

councils.name: Second Vatican Council
councils.summary: Renewed the liturgy and set out the Church’s teaching on revelation, on the Church herself, and on her place in the modern world, in sixteen documents.
